diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 2.2 constructs the finite surjective degree-two map pi:C -> P^1_k from the normalization/smooth projective model C, rather than from the possibly singular plane model X. Each of the four downward arrows denotes its restriction to the displayed closed-point fibre, with codomain the indicated singleton base point. Remarks explicitly specify this set-level convention; no complex topology or reduced scheme structure is asserted.

Step 4.1 chooses y_0 in k with y_0^2=f(x_0) nonzero. Algebraic closedness gives the root and characteristic not two makes y_0 and -y_0 distinct. At (x_0,+/-y_0), x-x_0 is a uniformizer, hence both displayed indices are one, using def-ramification-index-curve-map.

Step 4.1 and squarefreeness give f=(x-a)u with u(a) nonzero. At (a,0), y is a uniformizer and x-a=y^2/u, so e=2 and there is exactly one displayed point. Fibre-degree sum in lem-fibre-degree-sum-ramification-residue rules out further points.

Steps 3.1 and 4.2 use t=1/x and w=y t^(g+1). For n=2g+2, B/(t)=k[w]/(w^2-a_n) is k times k since a_n is nonzero and k is algebraically closed of characteristic not two. Thus p_+ and p_- are distinct and t is a uniformizer at each, giving e=1 at each.

For n=2g+1, step 4.2 gives B/(t)=k[w]/(w^2) with one closed point p_infinity, and t=w^2/varphi(t) with varphi(0)=a_n nonzero. The local parameter w gives ord(t)=2. The diagram depicts one closed point with e=2, without depicting the nonreduced fibre as two points.

Step 5.1 and local def-ramification-and-branch-points identify the branch images of the e=2 points. All residue extensions are k/k, and each fibre has index sum two. Squarefree f has n distinct roots in k. Hence even n gives n=2g+2 finite branch points; odd n gives n+1=2g+2 after including infinity. No commutativity, orientation or crossing relation beyond the four downward restrictions is asserted.
